sentences.text: Hungarosaurus was a quadruped with a body covered in hundreds of osteoderms, and it possessed unusually long forelimbs that were nearly as long as its hindlimbs.
The ornamented skull of this animal was estimated to be 32 to 36 centimeters long.
Mature specimens of Hungarosaurus reached a length of about 4 to 4.8 meters and weighed between 650 and 1000 kilograms.
Despite its large size, Hungarosaurus stood about 1.3 meters tall and weighed approximately 500 kilograms in some estimates.
Ankylosaurian fossils in Europe have been found in England, Austria, western Romania, France, and northern Spain.
The species was named by Attila Ősi in 2005, and the specific name 'tormai' honors amateur paleontologist András Torma, who discovered the fossil site in 2000.
Four specimens were collected from an open-pit bauxite mine near Iharkút in the Bakony Mountains of western Hungary.

Dental wear evidence suggests Hungarosaurus sheared its food rather than just pulping it, using a masticatory process involving an initial slicing phase followed by a retractive powerstroke with significant occlusion.
Cladistic analysis indicates Hungarosaurus is a derived member of the family Nodosauridae.
Hungarosaurus lived during the Santonian stage of the Upper Cretaceous, a time period spanning from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
